A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fast-FoundationStereo, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes supplementary Sections 6–15. The supplied material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot stereo evaluations, distillation and pseudo-labeling ablations, architecture-search experiments, pruning analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds supplementary sensitivity analyses, efficiency measurements and qualitative results.

M1.justification: The backbone distillation, blockwise search, refinement pruning, losses and pseudo-labeling procedure are retained. Section 10 newly documents vectorized implementation of the existing GWC computation; it does not establish that the method changed between versions.

E1.justification: Figures 13–14 add qualitative evaluation using Flickr1024 and DROID/in-the-wild images. This extends documented image coverage while retaining the stereo task, original benchmark suite and 1.4M-pair pseudo-labeled training set.

E2.justification: Section 10 adds a component-level efficiency comparison against the original per-disparity-loop GWC implementation. The full-model stereo comparator sets remain unchanged, and the new qualitative comparisons reuse existing baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a controlled refinement-iteration sweep at pruning ratios 0.6 and 0.8, efficiency profiling on RTX 4090 and A100 GPUs, and parameter, MAC and memory measurements. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged; newly disclosed search settings are documentation rather than demonstrated protocol revisions.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative cost-filtering pruning analysis (Figure 11), iteration-versus-pruning sensitivity (Figure 12), and intermediate pseudo-label acceptance/rejection cases (Figure 15). These substantially expand the supporting evidence about component choices, refinement capacity and data-curation failures beyond the retained Section 4.4 analyses.

E5.justification: The existing sampling of ten random architectures per latency budget is retained. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests. Its discussion of millisecond timing noise does not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores remain unchanged. New results include pruning and iteration curves, parameter/MAC comparisons, 0.63 GB peak memory, and RTX 4090/A100 runtimes of 30/41 ms for the proposed model versus 295/308 ms for FoundationStereo. Section 10 reports approximately 6× faster GWC construction and 3× lower memory use; Figures 13–15 add qualitative and diagnostic outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2), the blockwise formulation and the search-complexity argument are unchanged. Supplementary tensor shapes and concrete search-space counts add implementation detail without new formal assumptions, proofs or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: strong zero-shot stereo generalization at real-time speed through three acceleration strategies and pseudo-labeled training data. Supplementary evidence does not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: Section 8 interprets weak iteration gains under aggressive pruning as limited refinement capacity. Section 14 explicitly identifies inherited difficulties with translucent surfaces and suggests targeted training data. Section 11 adds an interpretation of memory requirements in relation to edge-device deployment.

D1.justification: v2 supplies detailed NAS options, 2,584 trained candidate blocks, 14 days of distillation on 128 A100 GPUs, selected latency/pruning settings, and the greater-than-60% consistency-mask acceptance threshold. It also documents vectorized GWC implementation and provides a repository pointer. v1's acceptance-contingent promise to release code, models and pseudo-labels is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to GwcNet, PCW-Net, DROID and Flickr1024 to support the supplementary implementation discussion and image sources. The main related-work discussion and positioning against efficient and generalizable stereo methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main paper remains nearly verbatim and preserves its section order. v2 appends organized supplementary explanations, limitations and acknowledgments, and removes the deferred-release sentence, without substantially rewriting the original narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 11–15 and Tables 5–6: sensitivity plots, efficiency tables, and extensive qualitative and pseudo-label diagnostic grids. Original Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–4 are retained, with only small pagination and text-flow changes.

improvement.justification: The supplement makes the unchanged core results easier to assess and reproduce through explicit search settings, compute requirements, filtering criteria and supporting analyses. It also states a concrete limitation. These gains are useful, although model specification remains imperfect: Tables 5 and 6 report 14.6M and 17.65M parameters without clearly identifying whether different variants explain the discrepancy.
